title: Handoff latency snapshot and SLO audit - Jan 10 2028
body:
Purpose:
Quick operational snapshot for the week of 2028-01-02 -> 2028-01-09. Focus areas: (1) handoff friction and page-response latency increase observed during two maintenance windows, (2) SLO audit for token-generation endpoints, and (3) follow-ups for on-call tooling (runbook clarity, paging thresholds).

Top-line summary:
- No Sev1s this week. Two Sev2 incidents during infra maintenance that increased 95th-percentile API latency for ~20 minutes each.
- Token-gen SLO (p90 < 120ms per token, p99 < 600ms) was missed on Jan 4 and Jan 7 during maintenance; rolling median unaffected.
- Handoff notes were incomplete in 3/7 rotations; caused delayed escalation in one incident (~12 min).
- Actions: adjust pager dedupe window, add a short maintenance-mode runbook, formalize SLO retrospective for token-gen endpoints.

Incidents (brief)
1) Incident: API-backend CPU pressure during scheduled driver patch - 2028-01-04 03:10 UTC
   - Symptoms: sudden p95/p99 spike for /v1/generate and /v1/chat-stream endpoints. Error rate stayed low (<0.5%), but latency degraded.
   - Root cause (initial): kernel driver update on a subset of GPU hosts caused an unexpected scheduler interaction resulting in CPU steal spikes and longer inter-process latencies.
   - Mitigation: rollback driver on affected pool, drain and reprovision hosts, enabled fallback routing to Dedicated fallback pool for high-priority customers.
   - Impact window: ~18 minutes from first spike to full rollback recovery.
   - Postmortem notes: hardware-driver compatibility matrix needs expansion; add pre-patch canary with load profile equivalent to 40% of prod traffic.

2) Incident: Batch-scheduler stall during autoscale test - 2028-01-07 14:45 UTC
   - Symptoms: request queue depth increased, some long-tail requests timed out. Observed increased KV cache thrash.
   - Root cause (triage): regression in batch-scheduler backpressure heuristics from PR #412 (see linked PR) that misclassified burst traffic as sustained, delaying worker spin-up.
   - Mitigation: reverted the heuristic change, temporarily disabled the new batching policy, re-routed queued requests to an alternate pool.
   - Impact: p99 latency violated for ~22 minutes; estimated customer-facing degraded experience for non-committed customers.
   - Postmortem notes: add automated unit tests for burst classification, and a load-sim exercise in staging for batching changes.

SLO audit snapshot
- Token-generation SLOs (service: api.token-gen)
  - Goal: p90 < 120ms/token, p99 < 600ms/token, availability 99.95% monthly.
  - Current rolling week: p90 = 115ms, p99 = 530ms, availability = 99.94% (one maintenance blip).
  - Violations: brief p99 breaches on Jan 4 & Jan 7 (counts small but above threshold for p99).
  - False-positive risk: maintenance windows can skew p99; need to tag maintenance-impactful traces and exclude from SLO unless notifiable to customers.

Operational handoff observations
- 3/7 shifts had minimal handoff notes: missing key context (which hosts are already drained, which runbooks were used).
- One late-night handoff missed the maintenance-expected-outage tag, resulting in pages routed to an L1 pager who didn't have access to the maintenance runbook.
- Suggestion: add a simple handoff checklist card pinned in the SRE rotation channel with three fields: "current drain/maintenance", "active incidents/mitigations", "escalation owner + slack ping target".

Runbook clarity and tooling
- The maintenance-mode runbook is currently a subsection in infra-runbooks > maintenance.md; it lacks quick rollback steps and a checklist for traffic redistribution. Draft attached below.
- Pager dedupe window of 2 minutes seems too short for some recurring flaps (we saw 3 repeat alerts within 90s); propose increasing to 5 minutes for latency flaps and keeping 2 minutes for error spikes.
- Observability gaps: we need a direct metric that ties driver patch windows to host-steal; propose a derived metric: host_cpu_steal_pct_by_driver_version. Add to SLO dashboard.

Action items (owner, due)
- Aisha: Draft maintenance-mode quick-runbook and publish in Confluence; include rollback checklist. Due 2028-01-13.
- Lin Zhao: Implement alert tagging for maintenance windows in PagerDuty so maintenance-exempt pages are flagged. Due 2028-01-12.
- Priya Kumar: Add burst-classification unit tests and create staging load-sim for batching policy. Due 2028-01-20.
- Ethan Murphy: Adjust pager dedupe window and run 48h shadow of new settings. Due 2028-01-15.
- Marco Rinaldi: Add host_cpu_steal_pct_by_driver_version metric and dashboard tile; coordinate with infra metrics team. Due 2028-01-18.

Notes to self / open questions (informal)
- Do we want maintenance-mode to auto-failover to Dedicated for all customers or only those with reserved capacity? Cost implications.
- How aggressive should we be excluding maintenance-impact traces from SLO? That affects transparency to customers.
- Can we add a simple play: "if p99 latency > 2x SLO for > 10m, route >25% traffic to fallback pool"? Need runbook & gate conditions.

Meeting syncs scheduled
- Quick sync with infra-driver owners (Marco, infra-team) Friday 2028-01-13 10:00 UTC to review driver compatibility matrix and canary plan.
- SLO retro scheduled Tuesday 2028-01-17 09:00 UTC. Invite list: eng-sre, serving-runtime, product-hosted-api.
- On-call tooling review with SRE/console team 2028-01-12 16:00 UTC.

Appendix (short links)
- Incident timelines (raw logs): JIRA-SRE-8091
- Batching regression PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412
- Draft maintenance runbook: CONFLUENCE-OPS-1423

Hand-off checklist (proposed, two-line format)
- Current state: [drained hosts / maintenance window?] | Active incidents: [list short keys] | Escalation: [owner, slack ping]
- Quick actions to take if page: [is it maintenance-tagged? yes -> follow maintenance-runbook, no -> follow incident-runbook v2]

End notes:
This doc intentionally mixes polished notes and quick 'notes-to-self' fragments; we'll convert the maintenance runbook draft into a proper doc once we collect infra owner input. Feedback welcome in the SRE rotation channel or directly on the Confluence page.
